$comment: <getopt.h> on every platform DSS targets (P68 round 9, D-CONFIG-NO-SHIPPED-GETOPT-ON-ANY-FORMAT). On Linux and macOS the platform C library's own getopt answers (glibc; Darwin's libSystem); on Windows no platform image exports it, so DSS builds it from shipped source (`runtime/platform/src/getopt.c`), written to mingw-w64's measured behaviour. main.c builds its own argument vectors and exercises: getopt_long over an argv with operands BETWEEN the options (a short option, a long option with `=value`, a short option with a separate argument, a long option with an optional argument), a missing required argument (':' with optopt), the PERMUTED argv and optind after the scan, plain getopt over an options-first argv, plain getopt over interleaved operands — where the platforms genuinely differ and each is held to its own reference (glibc permutes, GNU; mingw-w64 and Darwin stop at the first operand, POSIX) — and a `struct option` flag pointer. Six groups set six bits; the exit is 42 only when all hold. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 on x86_64 Linux and on aarch64 Linux (qemu), -O0 and -O2, exit 42; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 -O0 and -O2 exit 42, and so does the same program linked against DSS's `getopt.c` instead of mingw's; Apple clang 21.0.0 on arm64 and on x86_64 (Rosetta), -O0 and -O2, exits 42 too (the coordinator's Mac runs of this very program; Darwin's getopt_long permutes and its plain getopt stops at the first operand, as its arm expects). MSVC 14.51 ships no <getopt.h>.
